principles.principle: A claim is only useful if a stranger could grade it from public data.
principles.practice: Every Displace World claim stores the exact rule that grades it.

principles.principle: Freeze the claim before the outcome is known, and never edit it.
principles.practice: Each claim carries a SHA-256 hash; the engine refuses to save a changed one.

principles.principle: Date the event, the report and the check separately.
principles.practice: Signals show when something happened, when Displace published it, and when it was graded.
A coverage spike says many outlets wrote about a topic, not that the story is right.

principles.principle: Many articles can be one source.
principles.practice: Repeated wire copies are grouped before Displace counts outlets.

principles.principle: A probability needs comparable past cases.
principles.practice: Displace only prints a probability when at least 20 earlier cases exist, and shows the count.

principles.principle: Count misses as loudly as hits.
principles.practice: Misses are listed on the Trust page next to the hits.

principles.principle: A listed source is not a verified outcome.
principles.practice: Grades come from data (prices, counts, official records), never from a headline.
After a large daily move, the next week's moves are usually larger than normal; Displace measures how often.

principles.principle: A filing's item code says what kind of news it is, not whether it is good.
principles.practice: Displace reads SEC item numbers, not the filing's text.
Rule checkpoints are graded on whether the stated date held.
Every keyword-based link is labelled as such.
